programme: ATF4-driven integrated stress response (PERK-eIF2α-ATF4 axis) paired with NPM1-dependent nucleolar stress surveillance — a cellular stress-sensing/fate-decision circuit that shifts cells toward adaptive survival or toward proteotoxic collapse depending on load and duration.
role_in_a: In colorectal cancer, ATF4 is engaged as the effector of ER/oxidative stress adaptation — documented in a Bip-PERK-eIF2α-ATF4 axis mediating response to liposomal chemotherapy, in KRAS-driven ferroptosis evasion, and in ROS-dependent apoptotic responses to a natural-product fraction — while NPM1 is repeatedly reported as an oncogenic driver acting via AKT signaling, exacerbated by metabolic-syndrome/particulate exposure, and linked to CAF-driven extracellular matrix and immune remodeling.
role_in_b: In Huntington's disease, ATF4-associated integrated stress response is activated non-cell-autonomously and is curbed by stress-granule/condensate formation, and proteasomal stress-response induction (a downstream ISR arm) extends lifespan under proteotoxic load in a polyQ-relevant model; NPM1 nucleolar stress is reported to directly control mutant huntingtin toxicity and track disease progression, and to regulate neuronal survival in an expression- and localization-dependent manner.
shared_axis: Colorectal tumor cells under oncogene-driven metabolic/ER stress and HD neurons under chronic mutant-huntingtin proteotoxic stress both appear to rely on the same ATF4-ISR/NPM1-nucleolar-stress circuit to decide cell fate — survival and adaptation in the tumor, toxicity and degeneration in the neuron — so the module recurs as a general stress-surveillance layer rather than a disease-specific pathway, which is why the same two factors surface as concordant across cohorts of both diseases.
reasoning: Both carrying factors are independently and repeatedly placed in each disease by the retrieved literature (ATF4: 3 CRC + 2 HD papers; NPM1: 3 CRC + 2 HD papers), and the module is nameable directly from the factors (ATF4 = ISR effector, NPM1 = nucleolar stress sensor), so the record carries the account rather than pure inference. It stays at 'supported' rather than 'established' because no retrieved paper studies the two diseases jointly — the link is built by connecting two separately documented literatures, not by a stated shared fact.
support: PMID 41419319 (ATF4/PERK/eIF2α axis mediates ER-stress response to liposomal chemotherapy in CRC); PMID 42448954 (ATF4-linked KRAS-CCDC6-xCT axis driving ferroptosis evasion in CRC); PMID 42627401 (ATF4-associated ROS-dependent apoptosis induced by a natural-product fraction in CRC); PMID 39747204 (ATF4-related integrated stress response curbed by condensate formation in a stress model relevant to HD); PMID 37749371 (proteasomal stress-response induction extends lifespan under proteotoxic/tRNA-synthetase-inhibited conditions relevant to HD); PMID 41617421 (NPM1 drives CRC proliferation via AKT signaling); PMID 42304456 (NPM1 implicated in particulate-matter/metabolic-syndrome-exacerbated colon carcinogenesis); PMID 42554434 (NPM1 linked to CAF histone lactylation and ECM/immune remodeling in CRC); PMID 34880223 (nucleolar stress via NPM1 controls mutant huntingtin toxicity and tracks HD progression); PMID 27510036 (NPM1 regulates neuronal survival in an expression/localization-dependent manner, relevant to HD neurodegeneration).
how_to_falsify: In parallel experiments, knock down NPM1 (and separately inhibit the PERK-eIF2α-ATF4 axis) in an HD patient-iPSC-derived striatal neuron model and in a colorectal cancer cell line; if the same manipulation reduces nucleolar/ISR stress markers and mutant-huntingtin toxicity in the neurons but has no effect on proliferation or ER/ferroptotic stress sensitivity in the CRC cells (or vice versa), or if RNA-seq shows no overlapping ATF4/NPM1 downstream transcriptional signature between the two systems, the claim of a shared stress-response module linking the two diseases is falsified.
caveats: The tissue pairing is blood|colorectal and spans only 4 independent cohort pairs split into 399 patient-group comparisons, so the recurrence counts reflect repeated within-cohort subgroupings rather than 399 independent replications, and it is unclear whether the HD-side networks were built from blood/PBMC or CNS-proxy expression — a mismatch with the neuron/striatum-specific mechanistic papers cited for ATF4 and NPM1 in HD. ATF4 and NPM1 sit at 104/399 (~26%) concordance, well below the top-ranked factors PAX6 (203/399) and HOXA10 (168/399), neither of which yields a coherent joint mechanism from the retrieved literature — the most-recurrent factors and the most-explainable factors are not the same factors here. GATA6, RCOR2, FOXD1, PAX6 and MAFF each have single-disease literature support only and were left out of the programme rather than stretched to fit it. MYC and CEBPB, which would be the obvious bridge from MXD1 (an MYC-network member also on this list but without disease-specific evidence) to a stress/proliferation story, were removed as tissue-generic — their absence is the reason no MYC-centered account is offered, not an oversight. The single-view list (HOXB9, HOXD9, HOXD1, HIC1, HLF, KLF6, ZNF160, CBFA2T3, NCOA4, PPARGC1B, LMO3, TFAP2C) is dominated by developmental/lineage factors distinct from the stress-response axis, so their exclusion does not weaken this account.
